title: What your body does
subtitle: yawn, sneeze, chew, grin, shiver
summary: Name the things your body does by itself - yawning, sneezing, shivering, grinning - and use the right verb for each.

lesson.heading: The mouth and breathing
lesson.text: These verbs describe noises and movements your mouth makes, often without your deciding to. You **yawn** when you are sleepy, **sneeze** when something irritates your nose, and **snore** when you breathe noisily in your sleep.

examples.text: Why are you **yawning**? Are you feeling sleepy?
He **snored** in his chair with his mouth wide open.
It was so smoky in the room that he couldn't stop **coughing**.
She **sighed** with relief when she heard the plane had landed safely.
examples.note: a sigh is a long breath out that shows relief, sadness or tiredness

lesson.heading: Breath: three fixed phrases
rows: breathing very fast after effort: I ran for the bus and now I'm **out of breath**!
fill your lungs: He **took a deep breath** and jumped into the water.
keep the air in: How long can you **hold your breath** underwater?

lesson.heading: Eating
lesson.text: Six verbs for what your mouth does with food and drink. **Chew** and **bite** use the teeth, **suck** and **lick** use the lips and tongue, and **swallow** sends the food down.

examples.text: My granny used to say you should **chew** every mouthful ten times.
It's embarrassing if your stomach **rumbles** during an interview.
examples.note: a low noise from an empty stomach

examples.text: Take a drink of water to help you **swallow** the pills.
In an aeroplane, if you **suck** a sweet, it can stop your ears popping.
Don't **bite** that hard sweet - you'll damage your teeth.

lesson.heading: The eyes and face
rows: deliberately shut and open one eye, usually as a friendly or secret signal
shut and open both eyes quickly
draw the eyebrows together to show displeasure or puzzlement
go red in the face, usually from embarrassment

lesson.heading: The eyes and face in use
lesson.text: Notice the prepositions: you **wink at** someone, **grin from ear to ear**, and **blush with** embarrassment.

examples.text: He **winked** at me across the room to try to make me laugh.
Why are you **frowning**? What's the problem?
She was so delighted with the present that she **grinned** from ear to ear.
She **blinked** several times to try and get the dust out of her eye.
He **blushed** with embarrassment when she smiled at him.

left.label: shiver = because of cold
left.text: Small, fast movements of the whole body when you are cold or frightened.
examples: Look at him! He's so cold that he's **shivering**!
The poor little animal was **shivering** in the rain.

right.label: tremble / shake = fear, emotion, laughter
right.text: **Tremble** is small and often from fear or nerves; **shake** is bigger and can be the whole body.
examples: My hands **tremble** when I've been drinking too much coffee.
The poor little animal was **trembling** with fear.
She laughed so much that her whole body **shook**.

lesson.heading: Sweating
lesson.text: When it is hot, you **sweat** or **perspire**. They mean the same, but **perspire** is more formal. The noun of sweat is **sweat**; the noun of perspire is **perspiration**.

examples.text: We worked hard in the hot sun and soon we were **perspiring**.
It was so hot and humid that my shirt was soaked with **perspiration**.

lesson.text: Almost all these verbs have an identical noun form: to yawn - a yawn, to cough - a cough, to sigh - a sigh. The exceptions are to breathe (noun: breath) and to perspire (noun: perspiration).

exercises.prompt: I could see she was extremely cold because she was ___.
exercises.explanation: You shiver when you are cold.

exercises.prompt: She couldn't sleep all night because her husband was ___.
exercises.explanation: Snore = breathe noisily while you are asleep.

exercises.prompt: The fumes from all the cars and lorries were horrible and made me ___.
exercises.explanation: Smoke and fumes make you cough.

exercises.prompt: I knew I had caught a cold because I started ___.
exercises.explanation: A cold or dust makes you sneeze.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its definition.

pairs.right: draw the eyebrows together to show displeasure
crush food with the teeth so you can swallow it
shut and open both eyes quickly
deliberately shut and open one eye
use your tongue to take in food
make quick movements because you are laughing so much

exercises.prompt: The doctor examined my chest and asked me to ___.
exercises.explanation: Take a deep breath = fill your lungs with air.

exercises.prompt: Put your head underwater and see how many seconds you can ___.
exercises.explanation: Hold your breath = keep the air in your lungs and not breathe out.

exercises.prompt: We started running fast and soon we were both ___.
exercises.explanation: Be out of breath = be breathing very fast after physical effort.

exercises.prompt: He seemed very amused. He was ___.
exercises.explanation: Grin = smile very widely, usually because you are amused or delighted.

exercises.prompt: She ___ the stamp and stuck it on the envelope.
exercises.explanation: Lick = move your tongue across a surface.

exercises.prompt: I always find it difficult to ___ medicines.
exercises.explanation: Swallow = make food or medicine go down your throat.

exercises.prompt: Why is the person's body moving - because of cold, or because of laughter or fear?

items.text: He's so cold that he's shivering.
She was shivering in the icy wind.
It was so funny! I was shaking with laughter.
The poor little animal was trembling with fear.
She laughed so much that her whole body shook.

exercises.statement: It was so hot and humid that soon my shirt was soaked with perspire.
exercises.explanation: It was so hot and humid that soon my shirt was soaked with perspiration. Perspire is the verb; perspiration is the noun.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence about Mr Trubble's accident in a restaurant.
exercises.answer: I just bit an olive and I've broken my tooth
exercises.explanation: Bite (past: bit) = cut into something with your teeth.
